Overview: An app window is a view. A service owner holds a connection, identity or shared data. Hiding or closing one view does not inherently stop that owner.
Setup / example: Use the application menu for an app that is registered in this release. A registration file in a checkout is not evidence that it appears in the installed menu.
When Reticulum has no injected provider, its form says the service is unavailable and refuses actions. Configure the supported station-owned provider before expecting Connect to work.
Controls: Use explicit owner-provided Connect/Disconnect or Read/Check actions where present. Refreshing a view is not necessarily a new physical radio query.
Settings / defaults / storage: Registry declarations can supply app settings and required/optional dependencies. Availability and defaults depend on the actual registered release; the proposed general service manager is not documented as shipped.
Lifecycle: Reticulum session management starts idle. Saving or selecting a profile never connects the radio. Closing its window is not its Disconnect action. Broad desktop process isolation is not implied by an optional process-app experiment.
Troubleshooting: If a view is empty, distinguish missing provider, disconnected transport, no retained data and stale evidence. Do not enable a background collector just because its settings contract is proposed.
